/-!
# Andrews–Curtis conjecture

The Andrews–Curtis conjecture states that every balanced presentation (a presentation with the
same number of generators and relators) of the trivial group can be transformed into a trivial
presentation by a sequence of Nielsen transformations on the relators together with conjugations
of relators. It was proposed by J. J. Andrews and M. L. Curtis in 1965. It is widely believed
to be false, although no counterexample is known.

A balanced presentation on $n$ generators is modelled as an $n$-tuple $(r_1, \dots, r_n)$ of
elements of the free group on $x_1, \dots, x_n$; the presented group is
`PresentedGroup (Set.range r)`. The trivial presentation is the tuple $(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrews%E2%80%93Curtis_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- J. J. Andrews, M. L. Curtis, *Free groups and handlebodies*,
  Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 16 (1965), 192–195. [doi:10.2307/2033843](https://doi.org/10.2307/2033843)
-/

inductive Move {n : ℕ} : (Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)) → (Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)) → Prop
  | inv (r : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) :
      Move r (Function.update r i (r i)⁻¹)
  | mul (r : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)) (i j : Fin n) (hij : i ≠ j) :
      Move r (Function.update r i (r i * r j))
  | conj (r : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) (w : FreeGroup (Fin n)) :
      Move r (Function.update r i (w * r i * w⁻¹))
blocks.docstring:
An elementary Andrews–Curtis move on an $n$-tuple $(r_1, \dots, r_n)$ of relators in the free
group on $n$ generators. It replaces a single relator $r_i$ by
- its inverse $r_i^{-1}$,
- the product $r_i r_j$ for some $j \ne i$, or
- a conjugate $w r_i w^{-1}$ for some word $w$,

and leaves the other relators unchanged. These are the Nielsen transformations on the relators
(permutations of the relators are generated by the first two kinds of move) together with
conjugations of relators. The generators are fixed: no stabilization moves are allowed.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's FreeGroup / PresentedGroup / Subgroup.normalClosure (used for the presented group), Mathlib.GroupTheory.FreeGroup.NielsenSchreier (only the Nielsen–Schreier theorem, no Nielsen transformations), Relation.ReflTransGen (used to take the closure).
justification.name: AndrewsCurtisConjecture.Move
justification.why_needed: Inductive relation on n-tuples of relators in FreeGroup (Fin n) encoding the three elementary Andrews–Curtis moves (inversion of a relator, right-multiplication of one relator by a different one, conjugation of a relator by an arbitrary word), with generators fixed and no stabilization. Nothing in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib encodes Nielsen transformations or AC moves on relator tuples.

Two $n$-tuples of relators $r$ and $s$ in the free group on $n$ generators are Andrews–Curtis

blocks.docstring:
**Andrews–Curtis conjecture.** Every balanced presentation of the trivial group can be
transformed into a trivial presentation by a sequence of Nielsen transformations on the relators
together with conjugations of relators.

Precisely: for every $n$ and every $n$-tuple $(r_1, \dots, r_n)$ of elements of the free group
on $x_1, \dots, x_n$ such that the balanced presentation
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_n \rangle$ presents the trivial group, the tuple
$(r_1, \dots, r_n)$ can be transformed into the trivial presentation $(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ by a
finite sequence of elementary Andrews–Curtis moves (replace some $r_i$ by $r_i^{-1}$, by
$r_i r_j$ with $j \ne i$, or by $w r_i w^{-1}$ for a word $w$).

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma normalClosure_range_update_eq {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)) (i : Fin n)
    {x : FreeGroup (Fin n)} (hx : x ∈ Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range r))
    (hr : r i ∈ Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range (Function.update r i x))) :
    Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range r) =
      Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range (Function.update r i x)) := by
  apply le_antisymm <;> apply Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal <;> rintro _ ⟨k, rfl⟩
  · rcases eq_or_ne k i with rfl | hk
    · exact hr
    · exact Subgroup.subset_normalClosure ⟨k, Function.update_of_ne hk x r⟩
  · rcases eq_or_ne k i with rfl | hk
    · simpa using hx
    · rw [Function.update_of_ne hk]
      exact Subgroup.subset_normalClosure (Set.mem_range_self k)

lemma normalClosure_range_update_eq {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)) (i : Fin n)

    (hr : r i ∈ Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range (Function.update r i x))) :
    Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range r) =
      Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range (Function.update r i x)) := by

  · rcases eq_or_ne k i with rfl | hk
    · exact hr
    · exact Subgroup.subset_normalClosure ⟨k, Function.update_of_ne hk x r⟩
  · rcases eq_or_ne k i with rfl | hk

      exact Subgroup.subset_normalClosure (Set.mem_range_self k)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem Move.normalClosure_range_eq {n : ℕ} {r s : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)} (h : Move r s) :
    Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range r) = Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range s) := by
  have mem : ∀ (t : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)) k, t k ∈ Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range t) :=
    fun t k => Subgroup.subset_normalClosure (Set.mem_range_self k)
  cases h with
  | inv i =>
    refine normalClosure_range_update_eq r i (inv_mem (mem r i)) ?_
    simpa using inv_mem (mem (Function.update r i (r i)⁻¹) i)
  | mul i j hij =>
    refine normalClosure_range_update_eq r i (mul_mem (mem r i) (mem r j)) ?_
    have h1 := mem (Function.update r i (r i * r j)) i
    have h2 := mem (Function.update r i (r i * r j)) j
    rw [Function.update_self] at h1
    rw [Function.update_of_ne hij.symm] at h2
    simpa using mul_mem h1 (inv_mem h2)
  | conj i w =>
    refine normalClosure_range_update_eq r i
      (Subgroup.Normal.conj_mem inferInstance _ (mem r i) w) ?_
    have h1 := mem (Function.update r i (w * r i * w⁻¹)) i
    rw [Function.update_self] at h1
    simpa [mul_assoc] using Subgroup.Normal.conj_mem inferInstance _ h1 w⁻¹

An elementary Andrews–Curtis move does not change the normal closure of the relators, and
hence does not change the presented group.

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem ACEquivalent.normalClosure_range_eq {n : ℕ} {r s : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)}
    (h : ACEquivalent r s) :
    Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range r) = Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range s) := by
  induction h with
  | refl => rfl
  | tail _ hst ih => exact ih.trans hst.normalClosure_range_eq

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem ACEquivalent.subsingleton_presentedGroup {n : ℕ} {r : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)}
    (h : ACEquivalent r FreeGroup.of) : Subsingleton (PresentedGroup (Set.range r)) := by
  have : Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range r) = ⊤ := by
    rw [h.normalClosure_range_eq, eq_top_iff, ← FreeGroup.closure_range_of (Fin n)]
    exact Subgroup.closure_le_normalClosure
  unfold PresentedGroup
  rw [this]
  exact QuotientGroup.subsingleton_quotient_top

The converse of the Andrews–Curtis conjecture: a balanced presentation that is
Andrews–Curtis equivalent to the trivial presentation presents the trivial group.

claims.decomposer_note: Single universal Prop: for every n and every n-tuple of relators (r_1,…,r_n) in the free group on n generators with PresentedGroup {r_i} trivial, the tuple is reachable from the trivial presentation (relators = the generators x_1,…,x_n, up to order/inversion) via the AC moves — replace r_i by r_i⁻¹, replace r_i by r_i·r_j (j ≠ i), or replace r_i by w r_i w⁻¹ for any word w (permutations of relators are generated by these); generators are fixed and no stabilization move (adding a generator/relator) is allowed, so this is the non-stable conjecture; n = 0 is a degenerate trivially-true case; the article's remarks that it is widely believed false and that the Zeeman conjecture implies it are context, not extra questions, and the statement remains the positive Prop.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematically equivalent Prop: for every n and every relator tuple r : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n) with Subsingleton (PresentedGroup (Set.range r)), r is connected to the trivial tuple FreeGroup.of by Relation.ReflTransGen of the three elementary AC moves (r_i ↦ r_i⁻¹, r_i ↦ r_i·r_j for j ≠ i, r_i ↦ w r_i w⁻¹). I verified in Lean that inversion + right-multiplication alone generate relator permutations, so the move set generates the full (non-stable) AC-equivalence; every move is reversible, so c03/c07's reversed orientation and c08's explicit 'up to order/inversion' target are equivalent rather than defects; c04's extra perm constructor is redundant but harmless. Generators are fixed (no stabilization), matching the Wikipedia/non-stable reading. c05 chosen for quality: literal orientation (r → trivial), clear inductive Move plus named ACEquivalent, degenerate n = 0 test, one-move test, and API lemmas proving moves preserve the normal closure of the relators (sanity-checking the bespoke definition against PresentedGroup), which the repo requests for bespoke definitions. Copyright 2026 matches newest repo files; all declarations carry one category and AMS tags; compiles with only the expected 'sorry' warning.

context:
In mathematics, the Andrews–Curtis conjecture states that every balanced presentation (i.e. a presentation with the same number of generators and relations) of the trivial group can be transformed into a trivial presentation by a sequence of Nielsen transformations on the relators together with conjugations of relators, named after James J. Andrews and Morton L. Curtis who proposed it in 1965.  It is difficult to verify whether the conjecture holds for a given balanced presentation or not.
It is widely believed that the Andrews–Curtis conjecture is false. While there are no counterexamples known, there are numerous potential counterexamples. It is known that the Zeeman conjecture on collapsibility implies the Andrews–Curtis conjecture.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (tuple of relators, fixed generators, three elementary moves, canonical trivial target, non-stable version, n = 0 degenerate) match the source and were followed exactly.

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma normalClosure_range_update_eq {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)) (i : Fin n)
    {x : FreeGroup (Fin n)} (hx : x ∈ Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range r))
    (hr : r i ∈ Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range (Function.update r i x))) :
    Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range r) =
      Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range (Function.update r i x)) := by
  apply le_antisymm <;> apply Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal <;> rintro _ ⟨k, rfl⟩
  · rcases eq_or_ne k i with rfl | hk
    · exact hr
    · exact Subgroup.subset_normalClosure ⟨k, Function.update_of_ne hk x r⟩
  · rcases eq_or_ne k i with rfl | hk
    · simpa using hx
    · rw [Function.update_of_ne hk]
      exact Subgroup.subset_normalClosure (Set.mem_range_self k)

/-- An elementary Andrews–Curtis move does not change the normal closure of the relators, and
hence does not change the presented group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem Move.normalClosure_range_eq {n : ℕ} {r s : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)} (h : Move r s) :
    Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range r) = Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range s) := by
  have mem : ∀ (t : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)) k, t k ∈ Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range t) :=
    fun t k => Subgroup.subset_normalClosure (Set.mem_range_self k)
  cases h with
  | inv i =>
    refine normalClosure_range_update_eq r i (inv_mem (mem r i)) ?_
    simpa using inv_mem (mem (Function.update r i (r i)⁻¹) i)
  | mul i j hij =>
    refine normalClosure_range_update_eq r i (mul_mem (mem r i) (mem r j)) ?_
    have h1 := mem (Function.update r i (r i * r j)) i
    have h2 := mem (Function.update r i (r i * r j)) j
    rw [Function.update_self] at h1
    rw [Function.update_of_ne hij.symm] at h2
    simpa using mul_mem h1 (inv_mem h2)
  | conj i w =>
    refine normalClosure_range_update_eq r i
      (Subgroup.Normal.conj_mem inferInstance _ (mem r i) w) ?_
    have h1 := mem (Function.update r i (w * r i * w⁻¹)) i
    rw [Function.update_self] at h1
    simpa [mul_assoc] using Subgroup.Normal.conj_mem inferInstance _ h1 w⁻¹

/-- Andrews–Curtis equivalent tuples of relators have the same normal closure, and hence present
the same group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem ACEquivalent.normalClosure_range_eq {n : ℕ} {r s : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)}
    (h : ACEquivalent r s) :
    Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range r) = Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range s) := by
  induction h with
  | refl => rfl
  | tail _ hst ih => exact ih.trans hst.normalClosure_range_eq

/-- The converse of the Andrews–Curtis conjecture: a balanced presentation that is
Andrews–Curtis equivalent to the trivial presentation presents the trivial group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem ACEquivalent.subsingleton_presentedGroup {n : ℕ} {r : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)}
    (h : ACEquivalent r FreeGroup.of) : Subsingleton (PresentedGroup (Set.range r)) := by
  have : Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range r) = ⊤ := by
    rw [h.normalClosure_range_eq, eq_top_iff, ← FreeGroup.closure_range_of (Fin n)]
    exact Subgroup.closure_le_normalClosure
  unfold PresentedGroup
  rw [this]
  exact QuotientGroup.subsingleton_quotient_top

end AndrewsCurtisConjecture

items: A balanced presentation is modelled as an n-tuple of relators r : Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n) (same index type for generators and relators), following the standard treatment of AC-equivalence on tuples rather than sets of relators.

'Presentation of the trivial group' is `Subsingleton (PresentedGroup (Set.range r))`, given as an explicit hypothesis; since a group is nonempty this is exactly triviality. Verified non-vacuous (e.g. r = FreeGroup.of).

'Trivial presentation' is taken to be the canonical tuple (x_1, …, x_n) = FreeGroup.of. Trivial presentations with permuted/inverted generators are reachable from it by the moves, and every move is reversible by a sequence of moves, so requiring reachability of the canonical one (in the direction r → trivial, via ReflTransGen) is equivalent to any of the alternative readings.

Elementary moves follow the decomposition notes exactly: r_i ↦ r_i⁻¹, r_i ↦ r_i·r_j (j ≠ i), r_i ↦ w r_i w⁻¹ for any w. Permutations of relators, r_i ↦ r_i r_j⁻¹ and r_i ↦ r_j r_i are generated (e.g. transposition: (a,b) → (a⁻¹,b) → (a⁻¹b,b) → (b⁻¹a,b) → (b⁻¹a,a) → (b⁻¹a,a⁻¹) → (b⁻¹,a⁻¹) → (b,a)), so the move set matches 'Nielsen transformations on relators and conjugations of relators' without stabilization (non-stable conjecture).

The n = 0 case is degenerate and trivially true; included as a `category test` lemma. Added `category API` lemmas showing moves preserve the normal closure of the relators (hence the presented group) and that AC-equivalence to the trivial presentation implies the presented group is trivial (converse of the conjecture), as sanity checks on the bespoke definitions.

AMS tags: 20 (group theory) and 57 (manifolds and cell complexes), the latter because the conjecture originates in Andrews–Curtis's work on handlebodies and is implied by the Zeeman conjecture; a reviewer may prefer AMS 20 only.

The Wikipedia remarks that the conjecture is widely believed false and that Zeeman's conjecture implies it are recorded as context in the module docstring only; the theorem is the positive Prop with `sorry`, tagged research open.
